explain.say: In the summer of 1956 an English butler called Stevens takes his first holiday in decades, a drive to the West Country to visit a former housekeeper. As he drives, he remembers. Kazuo Ishiguro's 1989 novel won the Booker Prize. The board shows the gap at its heart: what Stevens tells us, and what we see.

explain.say: Follow his memories. In 1923, while his father lies dying upstairs, Stevens keeps serving at a grand conference, proud of his dignity. In the 1930s his employer, Lord Darlington, has two Jewish maids dismissed, and Stevens obeys. What does Stevens mean by dignity, and what does it cost him?

explain.say: Stevens is an unreliable narrator: not a liar, but someone who cannot face the truth, so we read past him. Sort the clues: he insists too much, he drifts into tangents whenever feelings come near, and other people's reactions show what he will not. When he denies ever working for Darlington, what is he hiding?

Look at the right side. With Miss Kenton, the housekeeper, there are moments of real closeness, but Stevens always retreats into professional politeness. When she tells him she will marry, he congratulates her and goes back to work, while she weeps behind a door. Why can he not say what he feels?

right.title: What we see
points: He loved her and lost her

explain.say: In 1956 he meets her, now Mrs Benn, and she admits she sometimes imagined a life with him. Later, on Weymouth pier at sunset, a stranger tells him the evening is the best part of the day, and Stevens weeps, then resolves to practise joking for his new American employer. Wonderful. Challenge: was his loyalty a virtue or his tragedy?

faq.a: Yes. He does not lie outright, but he avoids, excuses and reinterprets painful memories, especially about Lord Darlington and Miss Kenton, so readers must infer what he will not admit.
asks: Unreliable narration in The Remains of the Day

faq.q: What does dignity mean to Stevens?
faq.a: For Stevens, dignity means never letting personal feelings show while on duty, like a professional who never removes his costume. The novel suggests this ideal cost him love, judgement and a full life.

faq.q: Why doesn't Stevens tell Miss Kenton he loves her?
faq.a: He has buried his feelings beneath his professional role for so long that he cannot recognise or express them. He treats every intimate moment as a matter of household duty.

faq.q: Why does Lord Darlington dismiss the Jewish maids?
faq.a: In the 1930s, influenced by fascist sympathisers, Darlington orders the two maids dismissed because they are Jewish. He later regrets it, and Stevens claims he disagreed but obeyed.

faq.q: How does The Remains of the Day end?
faq.a: On Weymouth pier, after meeting Miss Kenton, Stevens admits to a stranger that he gave his best to Lord Darlington and weeps. He decides to make the best of the remains of his day and to learn to banter.
asks: Ending of The Remains of the Day

facts: The Remains of the Day won the Booker Prize in 1989.
Kazuo Ishiguro was born in Nagasaki, Japan, in 1954 and moved to England as a child; he won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2017.
The 1993 film starred Anthony Hopkins and Emma Thompson.
